A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, core method, and retained experiments. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, and relocated sections, figures, and proofs can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original watermark-detection, text-quality, robustness, and ablation experiments, plus infilling experiments and detector simulations in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds benchmark accuracies, key-dependent false-positive measurements, additional comparisons, and implementation evaluations.

M1.justification: The core optimization, expectation boost, predictive bias, and detector remain unchanged. Appendix H adds a SelfHash variant with H_t(omega)=omega_t and a diagonal-G token boost. Appendix I.1 implements the previously suggested optimization of computing watermark distributions only for tokens being unmasked, described as functionally equivalent.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual evaluations on MMLU, HellaSwag, ARC-C, GPQA, MBPP, and GSM8K, substantially extending coverage to knowledge, reasoning, mathematics, and code-generation utility. The WATERBENCH instruction tasks and C4 infilling evaluation from v1 remain.

E2.justification: v2 adds an evaluated GaussMark adaptation in Appendix C.4 and compares the original Unigram detector with the hypergeometric detector already used in v1. The existing Red-Green, Unigram, PatternMark, AAR, and KTH comparisons remain. Moving the Unigram/PatternMark comparison into Section 4.4 does not add comparators.

E3.justification: New protocols include benchmark accuracy at temperature 0.1, with random remasking and an additional LLADA-8B entropy-remasking configuration. Appendix B.2 introduces calibration on 10,000 unwatermarked, 200-token C4 passages. These substantially extend evaluation design; the original 600-prompt, temperature-0.5 instruction-generation protocol is retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of Unigram detector implementation sensitivity, false-positive calibration across keys, the SelfHash variant, and equivalence between standard and optimized implementations. These test detector reliability and implementation choices beyond v1's retained component ablations, text-edit robustness tests, and examples.

E5.justification: Appendix B.2 introduces a substantial assessment of variation across 100 watermark keys, reporting calibration curves and standard deviations of false-positive rates. Runtime reporting changes from 300 repetitions to five nonconsecutive batches of 300 and adds error bars. Existing shaded detection curves are retained, so uncertainty visualization itself is not entirely new.

E6.justification: Existing Table 1 detection, perplexity, and judge scores remain unchanged, but substantial results are added. Table 2 reports maximum false-positive rates at nominal 1% of 17.0% for Unigram versus 1.7% and 1.1% for the proposed contexts. Table 3 reports LLADA-8B average accuracy of 59.42% unwatermarked versus 55.97% with C={-1}, delta=4. New comparison curves and replaced runtime estimates further expand the results.

T1.justification: v2 explicitly requires no self-hashing for the factorization in Equation 2; v1 states this assumption only in the appendix's component decomposition. New Appendix H derives the joint token/hash objective and SelfHash solution, while Appendix G.2 adds Theorem G.1 and a KL expansion proof. The original principal theorem remains. The new KL derivation has a normalization omission in Equation 36 as printed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: the first tailored DLM watermark, its constrained-optimization formulation and ARLM connection, high detectability with minimal quality impact, and robustness. Additional evidence and qualifications elsewhere do not revise these headline claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges potentially non-negligible accuracy losses depending on model and watermark settings in Section 4.1 and Appendix C.5. It adds an explanation of fixed-key Unigram miscalibration and qualifies runtime comparisons because hardware conditions were uncontrolled. These materially extend v1's discussion of practical reliability and limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds keyed green-matrix row generation, bisection bounds and a 16-iteration implementation, GaussMark weight-selection details, benchmark evaluation libraries, and the optimized implementation's restrictions. Hardware disclosures and the abstract's code link remain. Documentation also regresses locally: simplified Algorithm 2 omits explicit iteration and energy-construction steps while surrounding prose retains obsolete line references.

R1.justification: v2 adds GaussMark, benchmark and evaluation-framework references, and citations supporting the discussion of fixed-key reliability and zero-shot detection. These extend the comparison with prior work, while the central positioning as a DLM adaptation of Red-Green watermarking remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose remains intact. The order-agnostic comparison moves from Appendix B into Section 4.4, Appendix B gains descriptive and limitations subsections, and implementation material gains additional organization. Local explanations, cross-references, and the publication header are revised without a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains accuracy columns, Tables 2-4 are added, and new Figures 6, 7, 16, 20, and 22 display additional evaluations. The runtime chart is redrawn with optimized variants and error bars. Figure 5 moves into the main text, and new or simplified algorithm blocks substantially alter method presentation. Most original plots are retained.

improvement.justification: The six-task utility evaluation and 100-key false-positive study address important gaps in v1's evidence for practical quality and reliable detection. v2 exposes model-dependent accuracy losses and qualifies runtime measurements, substantially improving the paper's empirical grounding. These gains outweigh localized regressions in Algorithm 2's completeness and normalization omissions in the new epsilon-parameterization material. The unchanged headline claim of minimal quality impact still needs qualification.
